Mr. V. Sh. Sharma, Advo  along with R-2 in perso  CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJNISH BHATNAGAR  ORDER % 21.03.2023 1.

The present petition has been filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. by the petitioner for quashing of FIR No. 252/2020 under Section 498A/406/34 IPC registered at Police Station Hazrat Nizamuddin and all proceedings emanating therefrom.

2. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 18.05.2018 according to Muslim rites and ceremonies and they lived together as husband and wife with each other.
Thereafter, the disputes and differences arose between them and they started living separately since October 2018.
On 04.09.2020, the respondent No.2 got the above said FIR registered against the petitioners.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, the parties have settled the matter amicably in terms of the Settlement Deed/MOU dated 03.12.2022.
A copy of the said Settlement Deed/MOU is placed on record.
Accordingly, the marriage of the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 was dissolved vide talaqnama/Mubaratnama dated 03.12.2022.

sentences.text: 4. Petitioner no. 1 is present in person in Court today and Petitioner nos. 2 to 6 are present through video conferencing.
Respondent no.2 is present in Court today.
Parties have been identified by the IO.
I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.
Respondent No.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioners.
She further submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily, without any force, pressure or coercion.
As per settlement, today, a demand draft of Rs. 4,00,000/- (bearing no. 166694 dated 08.03.2023 drawn on Kotak, Mahindra Bank.) has been handed over to respondent no.2.
Respondent No.2 submits that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
5. Learned APP for the State submits that in view of the settlement, the State has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
6. Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.

Consequentially, this petition is allowed and FIR No. 252/2020 under Section 498A/406/34 IPC registered at Police Station Hazrat Nizamuddin and all proceedings emanating therefrom shall stand quashed.
7. The present petition stands disposed of accordingly.

RAJNISH BHATNAGAR, J MARCH 21, 2023 p Syed Illyas Ali & Ors vs State Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187429991/
